definition: genus name.
rule: As printed in the paper. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed as '?stenophylla'".

definition: species epithet.
rule: As printed in the paper. Epithet only; infraspecific rank and name (subsp., var., f.) go in subsp. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed as '?stenophylla'". Hyphenated epithet is one word, no spaces ('novae- zelandiae' -> 'novae-zelandiae').

definition: Infraspecific taxon: rank abbreviation + name (subspecies, variety or form).
rule: Keep the rank word, written as subsp., var. or f. ('ssp.' or 'subsp' -> 'subsp.'; 'variety' -> 'var.'; 'forma' -> 'f.'); other ranks (e.g. nothosubsp.) as printed. Remove other marks printed with the name (e.g. '?'); printed form in notes. Never '*'; native or introduced status goes in native_status.
example: subsp. buxifolia | var. lanceolatus | f. glauca

definition: Full species name.
rule: genus + ' ' + species. Never include the subspecies, variety or form, or '*'.

allowed_values: native | introduced | exotic | naturalised | weed | as printed
definition: Whether the taxon is native or not native to the study location, in the paper's own words. The reference region (e.g. NSW, Australia) is whatever the paper uses.
rule: Use the paper's term, in lower case: from a symbol or code defined in the paper (e.g. '*' = introduced; code 'Exotic'), a table column, or the text. Unmarked taxon -> 'native' only if the paper says unmarked taxa are native; otherwise empty. Reference region in notes if stated. Use only the paper, never background knowledge.

definition: Plant family.
rule: As printed, in lower case ('MYRTACEAE' or 'Myrtaceae' -> 'myrtaceae'). Empty if not stated.

allowed_values: obligate | resprouter | O/r | R/o | O/R | code as printed
definition: Resprouting after full canopy scorch: proportion of individuals surviving and resprouting. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Map the paper's code by the paper's own definition, using VALUE_MAP: killed / fire-sensitive / obligate seeder -> obligate; resprouting (incl. facultative, e.g. FRR) -> resprouter; mostly killed, some resprout -> O/r; mostly resprout, some killed -> R/o; similar proportions -> O/R. Probable or possible codes (e.g. pK, ?K, ?fs, pR, ?R) -> the main class (obligate or resprouter); notes give the printed code, its definition and the certainty the paper states (e.g. 'probably' = 80-90% sure, 'possibly' = 50-70% sure, as defined by Kubiak 2009); if the paper states no certainty, say 'certainty not stated'. Code not defined in the paper -> copy exactly as printed, keeping its case and any '?'; remove spaces next to '?', '/', ';', ',' or brackets ('? r' -> '?r'); keep a space between 2 separate codes ('R s').

definition: Resprouting mode.
rule: Map the paper's term with VALUE_MAP (e.g. 'tuberoid' -> 'tuber'; 'basal bud' -> 'basal'); other terms as printed, in lower case and singular ('rhizomes' -> 'rhizome'). Several types joined by '; ', also when printed with 'and', 'or' or 'and/or' ('epicormic and/or basal' -> 'epicormic; basal').

definition: Primary juvenile period: time for plants regenerating from seed after fire to flower.
rule: Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in months. Then also fill time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4 (months / 12).

definition: Primary juvenile period: time for plants regenerating from seed after fire to flower.
rule: Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in years.

definition: Age at first flower production from seed. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Time or age to first flowering from seed, when the paper uses other wording than 'primary juvenile period'.

definition: Secondary juvenile period: time for resprouting plants to flower after fire.
rule: Fill only when the paper's term is 'secondary juvenile period'. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time to first postfire reproduction of resprouting taxa. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Time to first flowering or reproduction of resprouts, when the paper uses other wording than 'secondary juvenile period'.

definition: Maturation age: years for 50% of an even-aged cohort to produce their first viable seed. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Fill only for maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed, or from pjp_mths (months / 12, no notes entry). Time for 50% of individuals to flower goes to time_to_50_percent_flowering.

definition: Time after fire until 50% of individuals flower.
rule: As stated in the paper, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). Not maturation age. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time after fire until 80% of individuals flower.
rule: Time after fire until 80% of individuals flower, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity). Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time from fire until recovery, as defined in the paper.
rule: Recovery measure in notes, e.g. 'pre-fire cover'. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Unit of secondary_juvenile_period, time_to_50_percent_flowering, time_to_80_percent_flowering and recovery_time.
rule: Paper's unit. Empty if none of those 4 columns is filled. Mixed units in one row: unit of most values; exceptions in notes.

definition: Study site name.
rule: Copy exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section; do not add words (e.g. park or region name) or remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column 'A') to that name. Same site = same string on every row of the paper. Fill only if latitude and longitude are both empty, or several sites share one set of coordinates. Shared row for several sites: site names joined by '; '. Sites nested within larger sites (e.g. subsites E1 and E2 within site E): use the finest level at which the paper gives species data; a subsite named only by a code gets that code as printed (e.g. 'E1').

definition: latitude of the study area, WGS84.
rule: South negative. 33° 45' S -> -33.75. At most 4 decimals; no trailing zeros ('151.0' -> '151'; '-33.50' -> '-33.5').

definition: longitude of the study area, WGS84.
rule: East positive. 151° 05' E -> 151.0833. At most 4 decimals; no trailing zeros ('151.0' -> '151'; '-33.50' -> '-33.5').

definition: Rainfall of the study location.
rule: Mean annual if stated. Other period (e.g. post-fire year) -> period in notes.

allowed_values: wildfire | prescribed burn | experimental burn | as printed
definition: Type of fire.
rule: Use the listed values; other types as printed.

definition: Season of the fire.
rule: Several seasons joined by '; ' in calendar order summer; autumn; winter; spring (e.g. 'autumn; spring', never 'spring; autumn'). Only a date given -> derive the season and say so in notes.

allowed_values: low | low-moderate | moderate | moderate-high | high | extreme | as printed
definition: Fire severity.
rule: Map the paper's term with VALUE_MAP (e.g. 'very high intensity' or 'severe' -> high); printed term in notes when it differs. Term not in VALUE_MAP (e.g. hot, patchy): as printed.

definition: Assumptions, ambiguities, near-matches, page number of the source table.
rule: Items separated by '; ', in this order: (1) source location of the row's values, e.g. 'table 2, p. 342', 'appendix 1, p. 145', or 'text, p. 21' for values from the running text; (2) notes on this row, each naming its column where it has one, e.g. 'time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a converted from 43 weeks'; (3) paper-wide notes that apply to the row (definition of the code used, site, fire), written as the same text on every row of that paper, with no label such as 'Paper-wide:'. Page numbers as printed on the paper's pages (journal pagination), written 'p. 342'; only if no page number is printed: PDF page, written 'pdf p. 25'.
example: table 2, p. 342; fire_season_categorical derived from fire date 12 january 1994; code 'R' = majority of adult plants resprouted (p. 145)

definition: Full citation of the paper.
rule: APA style, in lower case (author names and title words too). End with the DOI as 'https://doi.org/...' if a DOI is printed in the paper; otherwise no DOI or URL. Same string on every row of that paper. No author, title or year printed in the document: file_name instead; nothing else.
example: benson, d. h. (1985). maturation periods for fire-sensitive shrub species in hawkesbury sandstone vegetation. cunninghamia, 1(3), 339-349.

definition: File stem of the paper the row was extracted from; links rows to the LOG.
rule: Same on every row of that paper.
